prompt: Write the body (about 150 words) of an insurer's answer to a personal injury petition in Texas: a general denial and three affirmative defenses that fit a sideswipe while changing lanes. Plain text. Call the parties only 'Plaintiff' and 'Defendant'. No names, placeholders, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1340; do not mention it.)
text:
Defendant denies each and every allegation contained in Plaintiff's Original Petition, and demands strict proof thereof as required by the Texas Rules of Civil Procedure. Pursuant to Rule 92, Defendant generally denies the allegations and requests that Plaintiff be required to prove the charges and allegations by a preponderance of the evidence.

Subject to and without waiving the foregoing denial, Defendant asserts the following affirmative defenses. First, Plaintiff's own negligence proximately caused or contributed to the occurrence, and under Chapter 33 of the Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code, any recovery must be reduced in proportion to Plaintiff's percentage of responsibility, and barred if that percentage exceeds fifty percent. Second, the damages claimed were caused, in whole or in part, by a preexisting or subsequent condition unrelated to the occurrence, and Defendant is not liable for such damages. Third, Plaintiff failed to mitigate damages by failing to exercise reasonable care to seek and follow appropriate medical treatment, and any recovery must be reduced accordingly.
